analysis.title: Global Reflections (Louis Miller, 6 Nov 2026)
key_insights: The post-midterm relief rally reversed the next day and pushed the market back into an AI-driven selloff. Frequent swings between AI and non-AI trades have cut conviction, and GS prime data shows de-grossing in eight of the last nine sessions.

GS vol panic index hit 9.57 out of 10, the biggest 2-day round trip on record. Cboe posted its largest put volume day on record. The US broad AI basket (GSTMTAIP) had its worst day since March 2020, and the TMT momentum pair (GSTMTMOM) posted its tenth -10pp day this year.

Global equities have seen de-grossing for a fourth straight session. Net selling was the largest in two weeks (-1.6 SDs vs 1yr), with long sales 2.2x short sales. Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 7.6pts w/w to 57.2%, the lowest since May 2025.

As positioning nears washout levels, GS likes owning the rebound in Hyperscalers (GSXUHYPR), where it sees the largest long-term AI monetization potential. It offers a Jan 110/120 call spread costing 1.8%.

Asia AI followed the US lower and clients added Taiwan tech downside hedges and shorted Korea and Japan. China Domestic AI (GSXACADO) held up better on policy support and national-team buying, and GS recommends re-engaging after the correction on compressed valuations and domestic substitution momentum.

US and European defensives just had their best monthly performance spread versus the market on record. GS recommends shorting US Staples (GSXUSTAP), which trade at their highest valuation premium to SPX in 10+ years with a dividend yield 200bps below the US 10Y.

For a growth-scare scenario GS proposes a dual binary: XLP below 97.5% and 10y SOFR ATMF below -0.15%, expiring 15 Jan 2027, costing 14%. European Staples (GSXESTAP) have a dividend yield 100bp above US peers but trade at 16x PE, similarly re-rated beyond earnings.

Energy prices reflect a higher probability of US-Iran peace. Brent is sub $100/bbl and TTF is down 17% on the week. GS argues the earnings gains of the Hormuz Bottleneck trades came from temporary factors that should reverse sharply in a peace outcome.

The European Hormuz Bottleneck basket (GSXEHRMZ) is up 30% since end February and trades 25% above its 5y multiple. Consensus expects 75% of the basket to post declining EPS over two years. GS recommends limited-loss implementations such as a Jan 95%/85% put spread costing 1.7%.

Equities had their worst day since Liberation Day but credit spreads stayed resilient. The generic 30y spread widened 2.2bps against 8bp implied by the 4.4% SPX decline. GS credit structuring says downside convexity has not yet kicked in and recommends shorting generic IG 30Y (GSIG30AS) against a beta-weighted long S&P futures position.

market_movers.rationale: GS recommends shorting US Staples on the highest valuation premium to SPX in 10+ years and a dividend yield 200bps below the 10Y. It offers an XLP below 97.5% and rates lower dual binary costing 14%.

sector_views.rationale: Valuation re-rate after the best monthly outperformance versus the market on record is not backed by earnings growth, and the forward dividend yield is at the 1st percentile relative to the 10-year range.
Trades at 16x PE (90th percentile over 1Y), re-rated beyond what earnings would justify.
Positioning is near washout levels and GS sees the largest long-term AI monetization potential here.
Valuations are compressed after a correction, domestic substitution momentum continues, and the basket is nearing start-of-year levels.
Earnings gains came from temporary factors that should reverse in a US-Iran peace outcome, and the basket trades 25% richer than its 5y multiple.

earnings_insights: Consensus expects 75% of the GSXEHRMZ basket to post declining EPS over the next 2 years.
The median stock in GSXEHRMZ is forecast (consensus) to deliver -11% and 13% EPS in 2027 and 2028, respectively.
GS argues the earnings improvement in Hormuz Bottleneck names (oil and gas majors, refiners, shipping, upstream chemicals) has been driven largely by temporary pricing and margin factors.
US Staples earnings growth is described as not enough to justify the current valuations.

trade_ideas.description: Short US Staples (GSXUSTAP). Dual binary: XLP below 97.5% and 10y SOFR ATMF below -0.15%, expiry 15 Jan 2027, costs 14%
trade_ideas.rationale: Staples trade at the highest valuation premium to SPX in 10+ years, with a dividend yield 200bps below the US 10Y and insufficient earnings growth.

trade_ideas.description: Long Hyperscalers rebound via GSXUHYPR Jan 110/120 call spread, costs 1.8%, 21d, 33v
trade_ideas.rationale: Positioning is approaching washout levels and GS sees the largest long-term AI monetization potential in hyperscalers.

trade_ideas.description: Re-engage China Domestic AI via GS China Domestic AI basket (GSXACADO)
trade_ideas.rationale: Compressed valuations after the correction and continued momentum behind domestic substitution.

trade_ideas.description: GSXEHRMZ Jan 95%/85% put spread, costs 1.7%, 24d, 5.9x pay-out (indicative), as a limited-loss way to position for an Iran resolution
trade_ideas.rationale: Basket earnings gains were driven by temporary factors that should reverse sharply in a peace outcome, and the basket trades 25% richer than its 5y multiple.
trade_ideas.risk: A not insignificant tail risk to the trade, which is why GS recommends limited-loss implementations.

trade_ideas.description: Sell $500mm GSIG30AS on swap (rates hedged) vs buy ~143 contracts of ESZ6
trade_ideas.rationale: Credit downside convexity has not yet kicked in, and in a systematic risk-off scenario credit would underperform equity.

risk_factors: Continued AI versus non-AI trade volatility reducing investor conviction and driving further de-grossing.
A systematic risk-off scenario in which credit spreads catch up and underperform equity.
Tail risk to the Hormuz Bottleneck short if US-Iran peace talks fail.
Growth scare, which is the scenario the Staples dual binary is built for.
charts_described: China Domestic AI (GSXACADO) chart: after correcting ~55 from its summer highs, the basket is nearing start-of-year levels.
US Staples (GSXUSTAP) chart: significantly outperformed SPX, and historically the next 3 months have had a negative relative return.
Staples forward dividend yield is at the 1st percentile relative to the 10 yr.
Correlation of XLP to 10yr yields is at local lows across 1m, 3m and 6m tenors.
Credit chart: amid the equity selloff, credit downside convexity did not kick in.
vol_and_positioning: GS vol panic index surged to 9.57 out of 10, the biggest 2-day round trip on record after Wednesday's post-midterm relief.
Cboe posted its largest put volume day on record.
Global equities saw de-grossing for a fourth straight session. Net selling was the largest in two weeks (-1.6 SDs vs 1yr), driven by long sales 2.2x short sales.
Fundamental L/S net leverage (beta-adjusted) fell 7.6pts w/w to 57.2%, down 14.1pts YTD, the lowest since May 2025 (4th percentile 3Y, 19th percentile 5Y).
Overall Prime book net leverage is at the 4th percentile on a 1Y view and the 37th percentile on a 5Y view.
Clients shifted toward Taiwan tech downside hedges (GSXATTXT, GSXATXTM) and short selling across Korea and Japan.
XLP correlation to 10yr yields is at local lows across 1m, 3m and 6m tenors, per chart caption.
geopolitical: Price action in energy reflects an increased probability of US-Iran peace.
Bloomberg reports US-Qatar talks on de-escalating tensions in the region.
Iran is showing a willingness to discuss issues related to its nuclear program, previously off the table.
Strait of Hormuz traffic flow potential is picking up, per the GSXEHRMZ chart caption.
